correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every neighborhood inequality to Y-y_i>=1 and X-x_i>=1. Each shore has sum at least two; a shore of sum two contains no label 2 and, for n>=4, contains a label -1. Rescue then forces the opposite shore to contain a 2 but no -1, making its sum at least n+1 and excluding total weight below six (and excluding a 2+4 split at equality). Explicit parity constructions attain six. Equality forces shore sums three, from which the label counts and all rescue-index restrictions follow. Exhaustive direct-definition replay for n=3..8 matches the theorem and minimum counts; the computation is corroborative, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard dense regular bipartite family and a natural structured perturbation of K_{n,n}. The result gives a complete exact value and optimizer census, and exhibits a sharp increase from the known complete-bipartite baseline to six after deleting one perfect matching. This is a natural family classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice or routine parameter substitution.
